issue_context.title: `series.str.cat(series.str)` is concatenating only the largest string
issue_context.body:
#### Code Sample, a copy-pastable example if possible

```python
import pandas as pd

arr = ["AbC", "de", "FGHI", "j", "kLLLm"]

ps = pd.Series(arr)
expect = ps.str.cat(others=ps.str)
print(expect)
Out[16]:
0           NaN
1           NaN
2           NaN
3           NaN
4    kLLLmkLLLm
dtype: object
```

#### Problem description
`series.str.cat(series.str)` is concatenating only the largest string in the series but it should concatenate all the strings element wise.

#### Expected Output
```python
Out[18]:
0        AbCAbC
1          dede
2      FGHIFGHI
3            jj
4    kLLLmkLLLm
dtype: object
```

comments: I'm not sure what's going on, but that's not my expected output. `series.str` is an accessor, not an array-like of strings. I would expect an exception to be raised here.

I'm very new to python and there might be some misunderstanding on my part. 

I believed the problem happens when passing StringMethods into `is_list_like` results in `true` ([code](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/4c778a1eb73da3a2935357dbbfcbe46f3be52f31/pandas/core/strings.py#L2110)). 

This happens because StringMethods implements the  iterator protocol ([StringMethod's iterator](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/4c778a1eb73da3a2935357dbbfcbe46f3be52f31/pandas/core/strings.py#L1986), [is_list_like implementation](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/4c778a1eb73da3a2935357dbbfcbe46f3be52f31/pandas/_libs/lib.pyx#L890))
For the OP you probably just want `expect = ps.str.cat(others=ps)`. @boomsquared if you have an idea of why this doesn't raise and would like to submit a PR would certainly welcome one
@WillAyd Thanks! Will give it a go
Like suggested in the PR discussion, I will implement a DeprecationWarning for `Series.str.__iter__`
Fyi: A `FutureWarning` was added and `Series.str.__iter__` will be removed in a few versions. Until then, the issue remains open though, so we don't close it.
@SaturnFromTitan this can still be addressed independently right?

review_comments: Not sure about this. I *think* the real issue is that `is_list_like` returns True for `s.str` when it shouldn't, though I do see that is also technically Iterable so maybe this should be allowed and just fixed
